You read that correctly. Sources from three countries confirm that the Trump Administration has advocated Viktor Orbán for the role of United Nations Secretary-General. The U.S. has encouraged the former Hungarian Prime Minister to enter the race, even bringing him the initial idea. The plan awaits a final decision.
A Trump State Department official concedes that it sounds crazy at first. But Russia and China are believed to be supportive, based on prior conversations with Washington, and the plan would be for Mr. Orbán to be their joint candidate. As officials from the U.S. and a second country told us, when the U.S., Russia and China all want the same thing at the U.N. Security Council, they usually get it.

articles.title_zh: Iran talks Middle East security, urges region to get US influence out
articles.content_orig:
Footage from a polling station in Rio de Janeiro showed electoral officials retrieving the voting results reports and disconnecting the machines after the first round of voting on Oct. 4, 2026. (Reuters)
SAO PAULO, Brazil— About 125 million Brazilians voted Oct. 4 on machines that print no paper ballots. Less than four hours after polls closed, the country knew its presidential election was headed to a runoff between conservative challenger Flavio Bolsonaro and leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva .
That process has been in place for over three decades, and Brazilians have become accustomed to its speed, simplicity, accuracy and routine. The system is robustly audited, completely disconnected from the Internet, and is the largest digital voting system deployed on the planet.
Eleven days before the U.S. midterms, Brazil’s system, analysts say, could offer Americans a more secure way to vote.
The system has been widely praised and was also mentioned in President Donald Trump’s 2025 executive order on elections , where he cited Brazil’s biometric voter identification as an example. Yet Brazil’s count runs partially on the kind of paperless machines that the president has vowed to scrap.
STATE DEPARTMENT CONSIDERS SHARING PASSPORT RECORDS FOR VOTER CITIZENSHIP CHECKS
Election workers prepare and seal electronic voting machines ahead of the upcoming general elections in Brasilia, Brazil, on Sept. 23, 2026. (Mateus Bonomi/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Over the years, Brazil merged federal, state and municipal databases into a digital voting record, whereby voter identity, eligibility and single ability to vote can (and usually must) be verified biometrically. Nearly 9 in 10 voters unlock the machines with a fingerprint.
Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court, or TSE, which designs the machines and oversees elections, says there has been no proven fraud since their 1996 debut. The 499,248 machines used on Oct. 4 never connected to the internet. Their software was open to inspection by parties, universities and watchdogs for 11 months before being digitally signed and sealed in public. Last December, the Brazilian government invited a record 149 outsiders to try to break the system; evaluators concluded nothing they found could alter results or reveal how anyone voted.
An electronic voting machine at a Regional Electoral Court (TRE) facility in Brasilia, Brazil, on Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. (Ton Molina/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
On election day, randomly drawn machines are fed paper ballots on camera as federal auditors and foreign observers watch and specifically track results.
Meanwhile, at closing, every machine used at every polling station prints its tally, which is then posted in front of the polling place with a QR code, so anyone can check it against the national count. In an email to Fox News Digital, TSE said each file’s digital signature "confirms that the result was produced by the electronic voting machine registered for that polling station."
Karina Stange Calandrin, a political scientist and professor at Instituto Brasileiro de Mercado de Capitais (IBMEC), says the system combines three traits rarely found together: voting is electronic, votes hashed to voter eligibility are stored locally in the machine and tallying is automated.
"It is an extremely secure and safe system. The machines never connect to the Internet and even the central database system used to transmit tallied votes to TSE must match results issued physically and locally by each individual machine without human interference," she said. Corrupting it, she added, would require breaking the seal of each machine and installing software that wouldn’t match the TSE’s version, automatically disqualifying its tally — a scale of collusion so large that it "simply could not pass undetected."
COLOMBIA'S 'EL TIGRE' SECURES PRESIDENCY AS LEFTIST RIVAL FINALLY CONCEDES DEFEAT
Brazil's right-wing senator and presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party (PL) gestures next to federal deputy and candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro, Douglas Ruas (L) during a campaign rally on the eve of the general election, in Campo Grande neighborhood, in the western zone of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil on October 3, 2026. Brazilians go to the polls on Oct. 4, 2026. (Douglas SHINEIDR / AFP via Getty Images)
The machines passed their toughest political test in 2022, when former President Jair Bolsonaro , now serving a 27-year sentence for plotting to overturn his 2022 defeat, spent years attacking their credibility without evidence. Bolsonaro is presently serving time under house arrest.
This year, for the first time, a Bolsonaro appointee ran the TSE: Justice Kassio Nunes Marques. Bolsonaro’s eldest son, Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, finished first with 47% to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s 45%. The machines at the center of the senior Bolsonaro’s controversy may yet hand victory to his son.
Florencia Ferrer, CEO of e-stategiapublica, which has audited elections in 17 countries, has no doubt the Brazilian system is the most modern and secure in the world. "In India votes are electronic, but each voter gets a printed version of their vote to take home, which weakens voter safety and augments coercion rates," she says, adding that Estonia’s internet voting and the Philippines’ electronically tallied paper ballots carry their own risks.
An engineer from the University of São Paulo’s Polytechnic School who audited the machines in 2014, and declined to be named due to the sensitive nature of his work, agreed. "While no system is completely infallible... we have found no traces of tampering, wrong-doing or malicious intent," he told Fox News Digital.
Still, some defend higher scrutiny. Security researchers say a clean record is not proof enough, and the Carter Center said voters should at least see a printed version of their ballot deposited into a separate area of the machine; otherwise, results integrity rests on software alone. Germany’s top court ruled in 2009 that voters must be able to check their ballot without expert help, effectively barring a Brazilian-like system.
Brazil’s machine has traveled mostly on loan to countries in Latin America , Africa and Asia. Paraguay adopted it permanently in 2006, with machines that now print each individual vote.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Brazil's President and presidential candidate Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (C) waves next to Vice-President Geraldo Alckmin (L) and to his candidate for São Paulo's governor, Fernando Haddad during a campaign rally on the eve of the general election, in São Paulo, Brazil on October 3, 2026. Brazilians go to the polls on Oct. 4, 2026, (Luis Robayo/AFP Via Getty Images)
"It’s obvious Washington and the remainder of the U.S. are way behind both technology as well as security when it comes to polling on voting day," Ferrer said. U.S. elections are run in thousands of local jurisdictions under 50 sets of state rules and about 30% of 2024 ballots came by mail , which is slower to process. Brazil has one national election authority, compulsory voting and no mail-in ballots.
Brazilians will vote this coming Sunday on Oct. 25. The winner is expected to be known and certified in under five hours.
"The question is not whether Brazil has invented a perfect voting machine. No voting system is perfect. It is whether democracies can combine the speed and consistency of digital tabulation with independent verification, public scrutiny and rules that citizens across the political spectrum have reason to trust," Ferrer said.
Solly Boussidan is an international journalist covering Latin America for Fox News Digital. He has previously covered international affairs, war, finance and travel for several U.S. and international outlets. He is currently based in Brazil.

articles.title_zh: S&P 500 rises as chip stocks gain for a second day, oil prices ease: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Crude oil prices fell for the second session Tuesday driven by a diplomatic push to de-escalate tensions between Saudi Arabia and Iran.
Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, were down 1.3% to $114.28 a barrel as of 10:32 a.m. ET. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures were 1.2% lower to $100.53 a barrel.
Saudi Arabia's defense minister and Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian held direct talks in Tehran on Monday. Senior military and intelligence officials from Pakistan and Turkey, who are allied with the Saudis, also participated.
Saudi Arabia has come under repeated attack from Iran-allied Houthi militants in recent weeks. The Houthis have bombed energy infrastucture as well as civilian targets such as airports.
The Houthi strikes threaten to disrupt Saudi oil exports, which have proven resilient during eight months of conflict in the region.
Iran's Foreign Minister Esmaeil Baqaei said the talks in Tehran were a step toward regional security cooperation and further consultations are possible, according to the state media outlet Tasnim .
The diplomatic push comes as U.S. President Donald Trump said in an interview with Fox News on Sunday that he was approaching a decision on whether to strike a deal with Iran or intensify military operations, suggesting that additional attacks remained an option.
Representatives from Qatar, which has helped mediate negotiations between Washington and Tehran, also traveled to the Iranian capital on Sunday, Reuters reported .
Prospects of a diplomatic breakthrough have helped temper fears of further disruptions to global energy supplies, putting downward pressure on crude prices.
But earlier oil price losses were limited as the prospect of a lasting resolution appeared fragile, with Iran-backed Houthi militants continuing their attacks on Saudi Arabia over the weekend.
—CNBC's Justina Lee contributed to the report.

articles.title_orig: Live Updates: 8-month Iran war looms over Israeli election as Egypt wades into Saudi's fight with the Houthis
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: 8-month Iran war looms over Israeli election as Egypt wades into Saudi's fight with the Houthis
articles.content_orig:
What to know about the Iran war:
The Saudi-led coalition fighting against Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said Tuesday they had downed two ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh, the Saudi capital.
"Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi group toward the capital, Riyadh," spokesperson Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki wrote in a post on X .
Multiple explosions were heard in Riyadh on Tuesday, journalists from the AFP news agency said.
Residents received a text-message alert on their mobile phones warning of an "aerial threat" and instructing them to seek shelter.
This latest attack follows weeks of strikes by the Houthis, who claimed Tuesday to have struck a refinery in eastern Saudi Arabia.
A Kuwaiti State Security and Terrorism Criminal Court sentenced three men to death on Monday over an alleged plot to assassinate First Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Al-Yousef, with prosecutors accusing the defendants of spying for Iran, communicating with Iranian-linked entities and joining Hezbollah, two judicial sources told the AFP news agency Tuesday.
The court also sentenced eight other defendants to varying prison terms.
Those sentenced to death included cleric and National Islamic Alliance Secretary-General Hussein Abdullah Al-Maatouq and two other men. One of the defendants had previously been convicted of terrorism in 2016 and later received a pardon before being arrested again in April, the sources said.
According to Kuwaiti newspaper Al-Rai , the defendants were accused of communicating with Iran and entities allegedly operating in its interests, including Lebanese group Hezbollah, to carry out hostile acts against Kuwait following the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei on Feb. 28, at the beginning of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.
The defendants were also accused of joining Hezbollah, a banned group in Kuwait, while knowing its objectives, and of engaging in activities allegedly intended to undermine the country's political, social and economic order and harm its national interests.
Kuwaiti newspaper Al-Qabas reported prosecutors accused the defendants of attempting to use explosives to carry out the alleged assassination plot and spread panic. One defendant was separately accused of attempting to bring explosives into the country to enable the others to carry out the alleged operation.
The reported Iran connection forms a central part of the case, although the allegations against the defendants do not, on their own, establish that the Iranian government directed the alleged assassination plot.
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis claimed Tuesday to have struck a refinery in eastern Saudi Arabia.
"With the help of Almighty God, the Yemeni Armed Forces succeeded in targeting the Ras Tanura refinery in the Eastern Province with a ballistic missile," military spokesperson Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said in a post on X .
"The strike was accurate," he added, "and caused massive fires at the targeted site."
The alleged strike follows weeks of Houthi attacks against the world's top exporter of crude oil.
A resident in the nearby city of Al Khobar told the AFP news agency he heard explosions around dawn and then received a warning message on his phone.
"We got the alert on the mobile and then heard a very loud bang," the resident said.
The Ras Tanura facility along Saudi Arabia's eastern Gulf coast is home to one of the largest refineries in the Middle East and is a cornerstone of the kingdom's energy sector.
The complex has a capacity to refine 550,000 barrels per day. It has been repeatedly targeted by Iranian strikes, including a drone attack in early March that forced a partial shutdown of the refinery.
London — Two men have been charged with serious security offenses in Britain after being arrested in connection with the incident last month near RAF Fairford, the air base in England that had been used by the U.S. military to launch strikes on Iran, the U.K. Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said Tuesday.
Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, and Nouman Essghir, 24, both British nationals and London residents, were charged under the 2023 National Security Act.
Abdulkarim was charged with "assisting a foreign intelligence service" in September and "engaging in conduct that was likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service in carrying out U.K.-related activities."
The CPS said Essghir was charged with a national security offense after he "approached or was in the vicinity of a prohibited place and his conduct was for a purpose that he knew, or having regards to other matters known to him ought reasonably to have known, was prejudicial to the safety or interests of the United Kingdom."
Both men were arrested last week on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service in a suspected plot targeting the Fairford air base in England.
The U.S. embassy in Baghdad has shot down two drones, Saudi state television channel Al Arabya reported Tuesday.
An Iraqi security source told the outlet that air defenses protecting the embassy destroyed the drones.
The government-owned Iraqi television channel Al-Anbar reported that the head of Iraq's Security Media Cell, Saad Maan, said that explosions heard across the capital were the result of a drone being intercepted and shot down.
The drone's origin remains unknown, and no immediate reports of casualties or damage have been released. The U.S. State Department has not yet commented on the incident.
An oil slick in the Gulf has reached a beach in the United Arab Emirates, video from the AFP news agency showed on Tuesday, with experts warning it could threaten desalination plants as it spreads.
UAE authorities said Friday that they had "detected a tanker oil spill affecting Umm Al Quwain's beaches," referring to an emirate north of Dubai.
By Tuesday morning, footage shot by AFP showed workers cleaning up oil on the emirate's beaches, which had been shut earlier by authorities along with other beaches in the country.
Satellite images taken on Oct. 21 and analyzed by AFP show what appears to be a slick of about 70 square miles in that area. Three days later, images showed it had quadrupled in size to around 290 square miles.
Experts from NGOs including Dutch peace group PAX said oil came from the tanker GEM NO.2 after it was attacked on Oct. 9.
They warned the slick could affect operations at UAE desalination plants, crucial for supplying water to the Gulf country.
"Satellite imagery from October 26 shows oil slicks a few hundred metres away from the intake of the Naqaa desalination plant. It remains unclear to what extent this will affect the process at the plant itself,"  said Wim Zwijnenburg from PAX.
The British maritime security agency UKMTO reported on Oct. 9 that a vessel had been hit by a projectile off the UAE coast, causing a fire that was later brought under control.
Mohsen Rezaee, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said regional countries should not rely on the United States for security, arguing that Washington has failed to provide credible security guarantees.
In a post on X Tuesday, Rezaee wrote: "America has not brought security to any country in the region, and Washington's inability to provide security guarantees has become clear. Security in West Asia must originate from within the region, and any foreign intervention must be prevented."
The U.S. has military bases in several Gulf countries that repeatedly were targeted at the height of the war.
A Houthi official said Tuesday that the Egyptian parliament's decision to authorize President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to deploy forces to Saudi Arabia to help the kingdom defend against the Iran-backed group's attacks was a declaration of war.

articles.title_orig: Earnings live updates: SoFi stock surges on 'exceptional' quarter, raised outlook
articles.title_zh: Earnings live updates: SoFi stock surges on 'exceptional' quarter, raised outlook
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Third quarter earnings season is in full swing this week, with corporate results on deck from Big Tech heavy-hitters Microsoft ( MSFT ), Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and Amazon ( AMZN ).
Aside from Big Tech, industries from oil to chips to pharmaceuticals will be represented, as Exxon Mobil ( XOM ), Intel ( INTC ), Boeing ( BA ), Ford ( F ), and Eli Lilly ( LLY ) also open their books.
It's shaping up to be another strong earnings season. According to FactSet data , nearly a quarter of S&P 500 companies have already reported Q3 earnings so far, with an overall earnings growth rate of 29.5%. If that rate holds, it will mark the third straight quarter of earnings growth above 25%.
United Parcel Service ( UPS ) stock rose 2% on Tuesday after the courier posted third quarter results and raised its full-year guidance, signaling solid demand during the upcoming holiday season.
Revenue is expected to come in at $92.6 billion this year, up from a prior forecast of $91.2 billion. UPS also increased its adjusted earnings guidance.
Despite inflation pressures and high diesel costs, UPS is optimistic heading into the last few months of the year.
"US consumers remain resilient and the outlook for holiday demand is strong," CEO Carol Tomé said on the company's earnings call.
The company is in the middle of a multiyear turnaround plan aimed at cost-cutting and reconfiguring its delivery network.
JetBlue Airways ( JBLU ) shares rose more than 14% in premarket trading on Tuesday following the release of third-quarter results and guidance for 2027. The airline reported a loss per share of $0.60, compared to analyst estimates of $0.54. Revenue reached $2.81 billion, slightly below the $2.83 billion consensus estimate.
The airline posted an operating margin of negative 5.1% for the quarter. Operating revenue totaled $2.81 billion while operating expenses came in at $2.96 billion. The company's operating revenue increased 21% year-over-year.
Chief Executive Officer Joanna Geraghty said resilient demand and strong yields drove revenue ahead of initial expectations, allowing the company to offset more of the fuel cost increases than anticipated. She noted that Fort Lauderdale continues to deliver strong results even as the company grows capacity in that market.
Yahoo Finance's Brooke DiPalma reports:
Coca-Cola ( KO ) posted better-than-expected third quarter results and raised its earnings outlook, but the company saw slowing demand in its North American business.
Coca-Cola stock traded lower in early trading.
The company posted adjusted earnings of $0.91 per share, above the $0.88 expected by Wall Street analysts, alongside revenue of $13.4 billion, also higher than estimates of $12.9 billion.
Overall unit case volume grew by 5%, more than the roughly 3% expected. The increase was once again led by Coke Zero, which grew roughly 16% year over year. Diet Coke and Coca-Cola Light grew by 6%.
Boeing ( BA ) shrank its quarterly losses and generated cash flow in the third quarter, but its top- and bottom-line results missed Wall Street's expectations.
Revenue of $24.1 billion and an adjusted loss per share of $0.34 came in below estimates of revenue of $24.3 billion and a loss of $0.20 per share.
The company's commercial airplane unit faced higher costs in its supply chain and for production as well as a $700 million charge on its 777X program. As a result, its operating margin in that segment fell to -6.5%.
"Backlog reached a record $745B. The 737-7 and 737-10 FAA certifications and F/A-XX award are meaningful milestones, though BCA margin deterioration to -6.5% from Q2's -2.7% introduces uncertainty around the recovery pace," CFRA analysts wrote in a note following the results.
SoFi ( SOFI ) stock surged 10% in premarket trading on Tuesday after the online financial services provider lifted its 2026 outlook and reported strong results for the third quarter.
Here's what SoFi reported for Q3, compared to Wall Street analyst estimates compiled by S&P Market Intelligence:
Revenue: up 45.9% year over year to $1.39 billion, above estimates of $1.26 billion.
Adjusted earnings: $0.18, above estimates of $0.17.
Updated 2026 guidance: SoFi now expects net revenue of $5.04 billion in 2026, reflecting a 40% year-over-year increase. Adjusted EBITDA is now expected at $1.66 billion of adjusted EBITDA, and earnings per share are forecast at $0.61. Wall Street analysts were expecting 2026 earnings per share of $0.59.
The company also introduced 2027 guidance, guiding for $0.90 of earnings per share, which is above the Street's estimate of $ 0.82.
"We had exceptional Q3 results against the backdrop of any environment, but they are even more remarkable given how 2026 has unfolded," CEO Anthony Noto said. "Our focus is simple. We are adding more members, who are using more products, and generating more revenue per product to create the most value for our shareholders over the long run. In less than a decade, we have transformed SoFi from a single-product company into an everything financial app with eight different businesses each generating over $100 million in annualized revenue."
Whirlpool posted another mixed quarter as inflation and lower demand in North America took a toll.
"What is new and different is the increasingly inflationary environment that has happened from Q2 into Q3, as well as the impact of volume deleveraging which is driven by the softer demand that we have in the North America industry," Whirlpool CFO Roxanne Warner told Yahoo Finance, adding that the team is focusing on what it can control.
In the third quarter, the company reported revenue declined by nearly 9% to $3.68 billion, which was below estimates of $3.91 billion. The company reported an adjusted loss per share of $0.21, lower than the adjusted earnings per share estimate of $0.76,  per Bloomberg consensus data
Warner said that the industry hasn't caught up to the "full impact of the inflationary pressures from 2022," with inflation up 12% since then.
For that reason,  the company plans to raise prices for the third time this year, now by 7% in the fourth quarter. That follows its largest price increase in history in April, at 10%, and a 4% increase in its list prices in July.
Revenue for major appliances in its North America business fell 8.3% year over year to $2.5 billion, below Wall Street's expectations.
Whirlpool's small domestic appliance business fell almost 1% to $286 million, below the expected $314 million. However, the company said that in the third quarter, some items sold out, leading to roughly 40% year-over-year growth in US orders in October.

articles.content_orig:
On August 4, 2026, the UK AI Security Institute (AISI) published a report that detailed some concerning behavior it observed from Claude Mythos 5 during its testing of the model’s cyber capabilities. In AISI’s evaluation, Mythos 5 was given a capture-the-flag (CTF) cybersecurity challenge, in which it was asked to retrieve a protected piece of data (the “flag”) from a simulated network. Internet access was deliberately enabled (this was standard for AISI’s cyber testing at the time, but is no longer). The cyber safeguards we deploy with general release models like Fable 5 were disabled. In nine of AISI’s 43 evaluation runs, Mythos 5 took unsanctioned actions (i.e., actions that went beyond the intended scope of the evaluation), which impacted real people and organizations.
In this post, which is being published alongside an independent report from AISI, we investigate these behaviors from Claude Mythos 5 further, to understand what they reveal about the model’s alignment. Like AISI’s report, we concentrate on the transcript (the complete record of the model’s reasoning and actions) from a single evaluation run. In this run:
This behavior would have been flagged immediately by our production safeguards on Fable 5, had they been enabled. Nevertheless, this behavior is important to study because the underlying failures here are not necessarily specific to cyber incidents like these. They speak to wider issues with the model’s conduct in evaluation settings; our models’ desired behavior remains a critical part of how we intend to ensure they behave responsibly.
The other eight transcripts were similar to the one described above. In each case, Claude Mythos 5 departed from the intended method for completing a CTF task, and took actions that impacted the real world. From an alignment perspective, we judge the primary transcript (above) to be equally severe or more severe than these other eight. In particular, the primary transcript showed the greatest degree of deception, in the form of Mythos 5’s attempts at social engineering to get its code change approved. Given this (and the degree of the transcripts’ similarities otherwise), we focused on completing one more exhaustive review of the primary transcript, and reviewed the other eight transcripts in less detail. This allowed us to run a large volume of experiments on the primary transcript, and thereby understand the root causes of the issues in more detail. We replayed the transcript from various points, and experimented with altering parts of the model’s prior context to examine how new information would have impacted the model’s behavior.
We judge Claude Mythos 5’s misalignment in the primary transcript to be comparable in severity to the Mythos 5 incident we discussed on September 9 , in which the model uploaded a malicious package to PyPi during another CTF task. This assessment is based on our judgment of the model’s behavior in two respects: overreach , or how far the model went beyond the intended scope of the task, and dishonesty , or the extent to which the model misrepresented its actions or intentions.
On overreach, the misalignment in this incident was somewhat less severe than in the PyPi incident. Here, before it turned to an attack, Claude Mythos 5 tried several approaches that would have been within the intended scope of the task; a task misconfiguration made it difficult (or potentially impossible) for the model to pursue those within-scope solutions successfully.
On dishonesty, however, Mythos 5 went further than in the PyPi incident. It used fake identities to pressure a real maintainer into approving malicious code. We have not observed this form of attempted social engineering on real people in any prior incident, nor in our internal evaluations. We interpret this as a severe form of dishonesty, rather than some new form or category of misalignment: as in the September 9 incident, Mythos 5 used these tactics exclusively in pursuit of its assigned task, and did not pursue any goals of its own devising.
On both overreach and dishonesty, we consider the primary incident to be more severe than any of the cases described in our October 9 post . And, for context, this incident is of a very different nature to the OpenAI–Hugging Face incident that was recently investigated by OpenAI and METR. That incident saw several unique misaligned behaviors (like very large-scale coordination between agents to attack a production system), though it did not see a model trying to deceive an individual human in the same way.
Newer models appear substantially less likely to initiate the attack described here. We replayed the incident transcript with Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, and a general purpose internal research model that shows capabilities greater than Mythos 5.1. Those three models began the attack between 0% and 13% of the time, relative to 83% for Mythos 5. Our newest models also proved to be much less likely to continue the attack once they realized it was causing real-world harm. Across our testing, in the immediate next few turns of the transcript, Mythos 5 never once decided to stop its attack, and Mythos 5.1 did so only very rarely. But Opus 5.5 and our internal research model stopped spontaneously 10% and 67% of the time—and we expect these rates to understate the true likelihood that these models would have ceased their attacks, since our tests only examined the model’s next few turns. Although we can’t be sure, we suspect that improvements to our alignment training have helped to mitigate Mythos 5’s behaviors in subsequent models.
We worked with AISI to complete this analysis of Claude Mythos 5’s alignment. A small number of researchers at both organizations were permitted to analyze the full, unredacted transcripts; a larger group accessed versions with sensitive information redacted. We provided AISI with regular updates on the progress of our assessment, held joint research meetings, and, to assist them in their analysis, shared information not otherwise available to AISI, such as the outputs of our interpretability tooling. We timed our publication to align with AISI’s own report into this incident. Their independent report is available here .
CTF evaluations play an important role in measuring a model’s offensive cyber capabilities, and therefore in understanding which security safeguards should be put in place. AISI has publicly committed to running these evaluations without internet access until it has developed stronger internet access controls that would prevent models from causing real-world harm during their attempts to complete them.
The remainder of this post is structured as follows. In the first section, we summarize our overall findings about the alignment of Claude Mythos 5 in these transcripts. In the second, we describe our assessment’s methodology in more detail, before turning to our full analysis of the primary transcript. Then, we briefly address the other eight transcripts, before concluding with a wider discussion of how this incident compares to the others that we’ve recently documented.
In this section, we summarize our findings in more detail. As described above, Claude Mythos 5 turned to attacking a GitHub project after its in-scope (that is, within the rules) attempts to complete the CTF had failed. Its attack unfolded over nine “compaction cycles”—points at which the model summarized its progress and wrote notes to guide its next stretch of work. The figure below divides these cycles into four phases. In the first two cycles (“pre-attack”), the model mostly worked within scope, but began considering a GitHub attack increasingly seriously. At the start of cycle 3 (“starting attack”), it began scouting for a specific GitHub project to target. articles.title_orig: Climber falls nearly 5,000 feet to his death on Nepal mountain after reaching summit
articles.title_zh: Climber falls nearly 5,000 feet to his death on Nepal mountain after reaching summit
articles.content_orig:
A German climber fell about 1,500 meters (nearly 5,000 feet) to his death on Monday, a day after reaching the summit of Ama Dablam mountain, according to a trekking company operator.
Wolfgang Waschiczek, 57, was reported missing from Camp 3, which lies at around 6,200 meters. He had been resting after reaching the 6,812-meter summit on Sunday, before his planned descent.
"After a successful summit, he spent a night at Camp 3 on Sunday, and on Monday morning, his guide found him missing," Gokul Thapa, head of the trekking company Real Himalaya, told AFP.
Thapa said Waschiczek's personal trekking guide, Sonam Lama, had left him in the tent for a few minutes to return borrowed equipment, telling him to stay inside. When he returned, Waschiczek was missing.
Waschiczek's body was spotted by another Sherpa at Camp 2 at around 8 am on Monday at an altitude of about 4,600 metres, Thapa said.
The body was retrieved by helicopter during the afternoon and taken to Lukla, a town known as a gateway for mountaineers and trekkers heading to the Everest region.
It was then flown to the capital, Kathmandu, where a postmortem will be performed at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital.
"Once the postmortem is done, the body will be handed over to his family members through the embassy," Thapa told AFP.
He said this was Waschiczek's second visit to Nepal.
"He had come to Nepal in 2024 for a trek, and his passing saddened us," he added.
Two Japanese climbers died last week on another peak in west Nepal, the Reuters news agency reported .
Ama Dablam lies in Nepal's Khumbu region and is considered a technically challenging mountain with steep faces.
This is the first fatality on the mountain this year.
Last October, two climbers, one French, aged 65, and the other South Korean, aged 66, died during expeditions there.
This climbing season, more than 300 climbers are attempting to scale Ama Dablam.
Mountaineers have died on other peaks this year.
In July, famed British Nepali climber Nirmal Purja and nine other climbers were killed after being swept away by an avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak.
In May, two Indian climbers died on Mount Everest during a record-breaking period of ascents via Nepal's southern route.
In May, American climber Shelley Johannesen died in an avalanche on Nepal's Mount Makalu. Johannesen, co-founder of U.S.-based outfitter Dash Adventures, had successfully reached the 27,838-foot summit before she was struck by an avalanche at around 23,600 feet while coming down.

articles.title_orig: Column | I saw the future of driving in Mexico. It’s off-limits to Americans.
articles.title_zh: Column | I saw the future of driving in Mexico. It’s off-limits to Americans.
articles.content_orig:
The unstoppable advance of Chinese automakers into the Mexican market—which continues to see record sales volumes —has dispelled all doubt: they’re here to stay, and it’s only a matter of time before they begin assembling vehicles in the country.
Their motivation lies not only in consolidating their presence in Mexico and the rest of Latin America, but also in meeting, as much as possible, the requirements necessary to export their products to the United States in the event that the market eventually opens up to these brands.
One of the automakers with a global presence that is already acting in anticipation of the inevitable is Nissan, the sales leader in Mexico by volume, whose executives estimate that its Chinese competitors will begin manufacturing cars here within three years, while their entry into the U.S. market will eventually occur, though “not before five years.”
This warning was recently issued by Christian Meunier, the executive in charge of Nissan’s operations throughout the Americas, during a conference in Tokyo where he explained that the consolidation of Chinese brands in Mexico “will trigger fierce price competition that will force Nissan and other traditional manufacturers to cut costs immediately or risk losing market share,” according to a report by AutoNews .
Meunier added that the Japanese automaker has already begun restructuring its costs and product development to prepare for this new wave of rivals.
“We have a very ambitious plan in Mexico, especially to reduce costs and be able to compete with Chinese manufacturers when they localize their production—which will likely happen in the next two or three years—so we must be prepared,” he emphasized.
One of the first measures implemented by Nissan was the introduction to the Mexican market of a hybrid pickup produced by its partner, Zhengzhou Nissan Automobile Co.
The Chinese Onslaught in Numbers
With this decision, the Tokyo-based automaker joins an ever-growing group of automotive companies—such as Ford, General Motors (GM), and Stellantis—that are leveraging production capacity through joint ventures in China to compete in the local market with models imported from that region.
This trend has led to a situation where, by the third quarter of this year, nearly 30% of the vehicles sold in the Mexican automotive market originated from a Chinese assembly plant, regardless of whether they bear the emblem of a Chinese brand or that of a U.S. or European company.
Official figures from INEGI indicate that as of the end of September, China-based brands delivered 130,488 units in the country. However, it is worth noting that this data excludes at least four competitors that do not report their monthly results to the government agency, including BYD, the Chinese automaker that leads in sales in the domestic market according to unofficial estimates.
Experts estimate that total deliveries by Chinese-origin brands in Mexico amounted to 206,679 vehicles in the first nine months of the year. However, to this volume must be added the sales of models imported from China by other global brands—a figure that exceeds 149,000 units, according to INEGI.
This results in a total of nearly 356,000 Chinese-made vehicles sold in the country, while actual sales volume for the period in question would amount to just over 1,220,000 vehicles. Based on these estimates, the market share of vehicles manufactured in China—regardless of brand—stands at 29.2% of the total.
Nissan and the other global brands will be joined by Volkswagen, which confirmed in late September that the first units of the Lamando L sedan destined for the Mexican market have already rolled off the assembly line at its partner SAIC Volkswagen and are on their way, with plans to be displayed at dealerships across the country before the end of the year.

articles.title_orig: Voters in Israel are deciding whether to oust Netanyahu after 3 years of war
articles.title_zh: Voters in Israel are deciding whether to oust Netanyahu after 3 years of war
articles.content_orig:
Jerusalem 4:44 p.m. Oct. 27
Aaron Boxerman David M. Halbfinger and Leo Sands
Israelis flocked to the polls on Tuesday in a tightly fought election that pits the long-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, against a loose coalition of rivals determined to unseat his right-wing coalition.
By 2 p.m. local time (8 a.m. Eastern), with eight hours remaining until polls were scheduled to close, voter turnout was nearly 45 percent, significantly higher by that time than in any Israeli general election since the 1970s, according to the Central Elections Committee.
The election is Israel’s first since the Hamas-led attacks on Oct. 7, 2023, upended the nation and ignited three years of war. It also has the potential to be one of the most consequential in the country’s history.
Voters have a choice between two blocs offering starkly different visions. Mr. Netanyahu is seeking re-election at the helm of the most far-right government in Israeli history. His coalition of nationalists and ultra-Orthodox Jews faces a fractious group of opposition parties loosely led by Gadi Eisenkot , a former military chief of staff whose son was killed in the Gaza war.
Both sides are framing the election as a make-or-break moment for the country. Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition offers the promise of a more religious Israel with an ever-tighter grip over the West Bank and Gaza. His opponents are casting the vote as the last chance to preserve democracy and pull Israel back from the brink of becoming a pariah state under international sanctions.
Voting will close at 10 p.m., but is unlikely to deliver an immediate verdict on who will be the next prime minister. Opinion polls suggest that Mr. Netanyahu’s allies and rivals are roughly tied, and assembling a governing coalition in Israel’s parliamentary system could take weeks or months .
Opposition leaders led by Mr. Eisenkot have called for a reckoning over what they call Mr. Netanyahu’s failure to prevent the catastrophic Oct. 7 attacks. They also have pledged to repair Israel’s shattered image abroad , including by cracking down on Israeli extremist violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Mr. Netanyahu has resisted the establishment of an independent commission to investigate the Oct. 7 attacks. He has vowed to move ahead with overhauling Israel’s judicial system, a move that critics say could undermine the country’s liberal democracy. And his allies say they hope to permanently entrench Israeli rule in the West Bank and Gaza despite international condemnation.
The 77-year-old leader has dominated Israeli politics for decades. In recent days, he repeatedly suggested that the country could face annihilation without him in charge.
Here’s what else to watch:
Key issues: In a tumultuous campaign , several issues divided Israeli voters. Read more ›
West Bank and Gaza: As Israelis headed to the polls, Palestinians in the West Bank were under an Israeli military lockdown. Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza cannot vote in Israeli elections, but they may have much to lose if Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition stays in power. Read more ›
Election integrity: Mr. Netanyahu used racially tinged language to cast suspicion over high voter turnout among Arab citizens of Israel and to encourage his base to go to the polls. Election officials said Tuesday that there had been no indication of widespread irregularities.
Trump weighs in: President Trump has endorsed Mr. Netanyahu , praising him as an important partner in the war against Iran and saying anyone else would be the “wrong leader” for Israel. Analysts were skeptical that the U.S. president’s intervention would sway many voters.
Natan Odenheimer and Heedo Abu Laban
Arab voters could tip the scales as Israelis turned out in large numbers to vote on Tuesday in one of their country’s most consequential elections in decades.
Arab citizens, who make up about a fifth of Israel’s population, have historically voted at significantly lower rates than Jewish Israelis in national elections . But pollsters, researchers and activists expected Arab voters to turn out in force, driven to unseat a right-wing government that has enacted aggressive policies against them.
Arab Israelis are overwhelmingly Muslim, with Druse and Christian communities making up around 15 percent. Palestinians living in the Israeli-occupied West Bank are not Israeli citizens and cannot vote.
Recent polls suggest that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing alliance nor the opposition bloc is likely to form a majority without a partnership with Arab parties. Such a stalemate would leave Arab leaders with huge influence on the results.
“The stakes are too high to sit this one out,” said Sireen Jabareen, 30, a director of a rights organization that helps Arab prisoners. She said she would vote for the first time after previously boycotting the political system, which she views as discriminatory toward Arabs. “I don’t want to be the kind of person who clings to rigid principles when reality changes,” she added.
Many others have also stayed home on Election Day in the past, alienated by political leaders, convinced their ballots hold no sway or unwilling to validate a system that they say treats them as second-class citizens.
Arab politicians and local leaders are warning of voter-suppression efforts, through either disinformation campaigns or the presence of armed right-wing activists near polling stations in Arab villages.
Last week, Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud party announced a joint effort with another right-wing party to send 2,000 activists to oversee “voting integrity” in Arab cities and towns. The move was widely seen as an attempt to suppress Arab voters.
In the 2015 election, Mr. Netanyahu sought to prod supporters by saying that Arab voters were “heading to the polls in huge quantities.” After critics accused him of race-baiting, he apologized for any offense caused by the remark.
But on Tuesday, he tried a similar tactic, pointing to apparently high turnout among Arab voters and suggesting that they were “trying to steal the elections.” (Election authorities said there had been no indication of widespread irregularities.) Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud party released a poster showing a crowd of women in hijab, urging right-wing Israelis “not to stay home.”
Yousef Makladeh, a leading pollster focusing on Arab society in Israel, said recent surveys indicated that 65 percent to 70 percent of Arab voters planned to vote on Tuesday. That would be an increase of 12 to 18 percentage points over turnout in the 2022 election.
For the very first time, activists say, efforts to turn out the vote feel like pushing on an open door.
Omar Abu Siyam, a social media personality from Mu’awiya, an Arab village near Haifa, Israel, said that when he told his nearly 90,000 Instagram followers that he had changed his mind and decided to vote, hundreds of commenters responded that they felt the same way.
The most critical issue for Arab voters by a wide margin, Mr. Makladeh said, is the surge in violent crime within their communities, a crisis many say the police have deliberately neglected under Itamar Ben-Gvir, the national security minister.
“Arabs are terrified of what four more years with Ben-Gvir in office will do to us,” said Dr. Thabet Abu Ras, a political geographer who is advising voter-turnout initiatives across Arab municipalities. He added that discriminatory housing policies, resulting in a record number of home demolitions in Arab communities, were also driving voters.
Higher Arab turnout could threaten smaller parties that are more likely to support Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition. By increasing the total number of votes cast, it would raise the threshold for smaller parties to win seats in the Knesset.
“This time,” Dr. Abu Ras said, “the Arab vote is worth gold.”

articles.title_orig: Apple refreshes the iMac with M6 chips
articles.title_zh: Apple refreshes the iMac with M6 chips
articles.content_orig:
The all-in-one desktop computer has been updated with a more powerful chip.﻿
The all-in-one desktop computer has been updated with a more powerful chip.﻿
Apple is updating the iMac with M6 chips. The new iMac generation was introduced today, giving Apple’s all-in-one desktop computer a performance boost via the same chipset Apple launched with the Mac Mini in August . Prices start from $1,499, and the design otherwise appears largely unchanged. The update was announced ahead of Apple’s “Pro and Tell” event that’s scheduled to take place on Wednesday.
This refresh comes two years after Apple gave the iMac an overhaul with M4 chips , meaning we’re skipping the M5 series entirely on this hardware. That should make this upgrade more meaningful. The M6 is Apple’s first 2nm chip and includes a dual 16-core Neural Engine that can boost performance when running on-device AI tasks. According to Apple’s press release, the M6-powered iMac “delivers up to 5x faster on-device AI performance” compared to the M4 model.
The M6 configurations start from a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU for $1,499, which is the same price as the 8-core CPU-equipped M4 iMac. There’s also a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU starting at $1,699. Preorders will launch at 1:10PM ET on October 28th, and it’ll be fully available starting November 6th.
Besides the chip upgrade, the new iMac isn’t getting much in the way of a hardware refresh. It now has Apple’s N1 wireless networking chip, alongside Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 on the base model instead of just the higher-spec variant. It still carries over the same Thunderbolt limitations as the M4 iMac, however — you only get two ports on the 10-core version, and four on the 12-core upgrade.
There are also some new restrictions and fees included in the configuration options. If you want to customize the iMac with a Magic Trackpad instead of a Magic Mouse, it’ll cost you an extra $50, despite this being a free switch on the previous iMac. Ethernet has been upgraded from 1 gigabit to 2.5 gigabit, but thats now a $30 premium upgrade compared to sticking with a Wi-Fi only configuration. Apple also won’t let you configure the M6 iMac with a Magic Keyboard that has Touch ID but not a numeric keypad — despite showing an image of that on the new iMac announcement page.
If you were hoping for some new color options then, hard luck. Apple is offering the exact same color variants as it did with the M4, to the point where it’s just reused some of the marketing imagery and updated them to display more up-to-date content. The M6 chip provides a nice performance boost, but otherwise this is a small spec bump for Apple’s colorful all-in-one.

Ford’s upcoming electric truck integrates an onboard inverter to dramatically slash the cost, hardware, and utility red tape of home backup power.
Ford’s upcoming electric truck integrates an onboard inverter to dramatically slash the cost, hardware, and utility red tape of home backup power.
We’re still a few months away from the official reveal of the Ford Fathom , the automaker’s first next-generation electric vehicle. While we wait, Ford has been whetting our appetite with news about the sub-$30,000 pickup — including today’s announcement about the Fathom’s bidirectional charging capabilities.
With an increasing number of EVs coming out with bidirectional vehicle-to-home (V2H) or vehicle-to-load (V2L) charging capabilities, Ford is trying to position the Fathom as a key entrant — and one that simplifies the system by making it an everyday reality rather than a $10,000 luxury perk. Unlike the discontinued F-150 Lightning, which required a massive, expensive external DC-to-AC wall inverter, the Fathom packs the inverter directly into its onboard “E-box” to pump out over 10 kW of AC power natively.
The Fathom’s built-in inverter converts its battery power into standard household electricity to run appliances, back up a home during an outage, or feed energy back into the grid.
Taking advantage of these features will require additional hardware, though Ford aims to make it significantly cheaper than current options. To send power back to the grid, owners will need the Ford Home Power Station. Ford is targeting a 50 percent discount compared to the existing $1,310 Ford Charge Station Pro. For whole-home backup power during a blackout, owners must pair that station with a backup panel. While that combination typically runs around $5,205, Ford is aiming for an estimated $3,123 — a roughly 40 percent reduction — though finalized pricing for both packages is still pending.
The Fathom, a $28,000 electric pickup truck, will be the first vehicle on Ford’s new Universal Electric Vehicle Platform , an innovative new system designed to maximize aerodynamic range while also reducing production costs so Ford can make a profitable EV. For over a year, the company has been hyping it as its “Model T moment” that will revolutionize nearly everything at the 123-year-old company.
Another barrier to V2H or V2L charging is red tape from public utilities. Ford’s solution was to team up with five of North America’s biggest power companies — Pacific Gas and Electric (PG&E); American Electric Power (AEP); BC Hydro; Consumers Energy; and Exelon — which collectively cover millions of customers in the US and Canada. Ford theorized that whatever rules they agree on will likely become the standard everyone else follows. They agreed to cut the paperwork for basic storm backup, use common plugs and software, and make grid programs automatic.
Cutting the cost of the Ford Home Power Station and Backup Panel is certainly helpful, but homeowners will still face additional costs related to permitting, electrician labor, and heavy-gauge wiring. These could conspire to keep these bidirectional charging features out of reach for some customers.
Still, Ford is intent on keeping the costs low for its new electric truck. With supply chain constraints and trade upheaval, that will remain a central challenge for the automaker as it gets closer to one of the most important vehicle debuts in Ford’s history.

articles.title_orig: Prediction: The Stock Market Could Crash in 2027, and Elon Musk Just Explained Why
articles.title_zh: Prediction: The Stock Market Could Crash in 2027, and Elon Musk Just Explained Why
articles.content_orig:
The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC +0.14% ) has delivered unusually high returns over the last few years, largely thanks to the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution. Companies such as Microsoft ( MSFT -0.29% ) , Alphabet ( GOOGL +0.80% ) ( GOOG +0.52% ) , Amazon ( AMZN +0.36% ) , and Meta Platforms ( META -1.14% ) have collectively invested hundreds of billions of dollars in AI infrastructure, fueling a historical supercycle in semiconductor demand, data center construction, and cloud computing.
Unfortunately, there is a potential problem hiding in plain sight. The stock market has become increasingly dependent on a relatively small cohort of technology companies to generate outsize growth. If those businesses stumble, the consequences could ripple beyond the technology sector.
Image source: Getty Images.
On Oct. 25, Elon Musk expressed a troubling warning about the health of the AI infrastructure industry. His comments suggest that 2027 could bring financial distress, business consolidation, and a slowdown in data center investments.
This sounds like a recipe for a significant stock market correction , or potentially even a full-blown crash. Let's dig into why.
In a response to venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya on X (formerly Twitter), Musk warned that financing conditions are deteriorating for companies developing AI data centers. In his view, lenders are reluctant to finance businesses without meaningful revenue sources outside AI infrastructure.
This is particularly concerning for specialized cloud computing providers, commonly called neoclouds, which purchase GPUs and rent compute capacity to AI developers. Companies such as CoreWeave and Nebius have benefited from the AI revolution so far, but the next phase of their expansion plans requires ongoing access to outside capital.
Musk predicts that "200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation." Meanwhile, Palihapitiya warns that construction delays could leave significant volumes of computing equipment sitting idle in unfinished data centers in 2027.
What investors need to understand is that the implications here would extend throughout the AI supply chain. If neoclouds fail to secure financing or complete their data centers, they could delay GPU purchases. Moreover, hyperscalers would also likely moderate their capex if electricity shortages, construction delays, or disappointing returns prevent them from deploying equipment efficiently.
While this doesn't mean demand for AI will disappear, it does suggest that demand for compute could remain strong while the companies supplying that power still struggle to finance additional infrastructure. That's where things get messy for the broader stock market.
The S&P 500 tracks America's largest publicly traded companies. The index is weighted by market capitalization, meaning larger companies have more influence over its performance than smaller businesses.
As of this writing (Oct. 26), Nvidia accounted for 7.5% of the S&P 500, followed by Apple at 7.2% and Microsoft at 5.6%. Amazon accounts for another 3.8%, while Alphabet's two share classes collectively represented approximately 5.6%. Broadcom , Meta Platforms, and Tesla contributed another 6.8%.
Combined, these eight technology giants represent approximately 36% of the entire index. In other words, more than one-third of the S&P 500's performance depends on just eight companies. This concentration is the product of continuously rewarding businesses positioned to benefit from AI.
Nvidia supplies the GPUs powering AI infrastructure, while Broadcom develops custom accelerators and networking technology. Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta are investing aggressively in data centers to support their AI ambitions. While Apple and Tesla are less directly exposed to AI infrastructure, their enormous market capitalizations still contribute to the same concentration problem .
Let's consider what would happen if the eight companies collectively experienced a 30% drawdown while the remaining S&P 500 members remained unchanged. Based on their current index weights, that would translate into roughly a 10% decline in the S&P 500.
It's important to understand the magnitude here, because this is before accounting for weakness that would spread to other semiconductor companies, data center operators, utilities, and businesses exposed to AI infrastructure.
Of note, the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC +0.42% ) would be even more vulnerable due to its heavy exposure to technology and growth stocks.
The biggest threat to the stock market is not that the AI bubble pops, but that investors have already priced in more success than the industry can realistically deliver. In turn, growth stocks could be headed for a nasty period of valuation multiple compression.
For example, a stock trading at 40 times earnings that falls to 30 times earnings would lose 25% of its value, even if its underlying profits remained unchanged. If earnings expectations change to the downside, the potential sell-off becomes even harsher.
My prediction is that 2027 could be a difficult year for technology stocks, with the potential for a broader market downturn if Musk's forecast materializes. This reinforces the importance of staying diversified and buying stocks at reasonable valuations.

articles.title_orig: Vladimir Putin speaks with Norwegian and Finnish leaders
articles.title_zh: Vladimir Putin speaks with Norwegian and Finnish leaders
articles.content_orig:
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - a rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.
The aim was looking at "future negotiations to help to end the war" in Ukraine, the offices of President Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said. Their initiative was not on behalf of "Europe as a whole".
After the call, Putin said "confrontational" EU and Nato policies were prolonging the war which began when Russia launched a full-scale invasion in 2022.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has spoken to the two Nordic leaders after their conversation with Putin. Last week, Zelensky met them as well as US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo.
The Ukrainian leader said he was grateful for the "active support" of his Finnish and Norwegian counterparts.
Tuesday's 90-minute phone call was held from the Finnish capital Helsinki, and showed "big differences in views", Støre said.
Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the call to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.
The call was "frank and substantive", Stubb said, explaining that the war's outcome will "have a direct impact on our and the broader European security".
Støre added: "The war comes with enormous human and material costs... The suffering and destruction will impact generations."
The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders that "a just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered.
He - like Stubb and Støre - had agreed to continue their direct phone communication, the statement added.
Støre said all their allies had been informed of the call ahead of time.
Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she was "very sceptical" of Tuesday's dialogue, telling Danish broadcaster DR, it had not been "co-ordinated with any of the rest of us".
Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Stubb had informed him that Europe's position on the upcoming talks in the United Arab Emirates, was "moderately optimistic".
Relations between the US, Ukraine and its European allies have been souring since US President Donald Trump agreed to lift some sanctions from Russia - allowing it to export oil to the US.
But last week, Stubb, Støre and Zelesnky met with Witkoff in the Norwegian capital, before the US special envoy travelled on to St Petersburg to meet Putin.
Following the talks, Ukraine, Russia and the US agreed to resume three-way negotiations that Russia had stopped for months.
After speaking to the two Nordic leaders, Zelensky said part of their discussions with Putin had centred on November's trilateral talks to be held in Abu Dhabi.
Zelensky said he had discussed with them "various formats for our engagement with partners in Europe that could be useful in further supporting diplomacy, our defense, and our shared security".
Stubb and Støre are the first European leaders to contact Putin since French President Emmanuel Macron's conversation with him in July 2025.
As the US administration's position on Russia has softened, several European leaders have said Europe should be trying to establish direct contacts with the Kremlin.
Moscow regularly mocks European leaders and accuses the European Union of prolonging the war by supplying Ukraine with weapons.
But last weekend, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said having a European negotiator at the peace talks table would be "good".

articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Apple's iPhone Duo cracked screens days after launch, dropping shares 1% and leaving its $5 trillion market cap just $19 billion above the milestone.
NVDA climbed to $216, pushing its market cap to $5.215 trillion and extending its lead over Apple to $196 billion.

Apple's first foldable phone has just reached customers, and on October 26, 2026, the company admitted that some units are breaking at the fold.
Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ) confirmed a defect in the inner folding display of the $1,999 iPhone Duo. The phone reached stores on October 23, after preorders sold out within minutes on October 16.
Shares fell 1.1%, or $3.81, to $343.91, then traded at $343.64 after hours. Part of that decline came from a bearish Jefferies note ahead of earnings and from a reaction to a pricier iPad mini, so the cracks add a new drag on pressure that was already there.
Apple is worth $5.019 trillion. That is roughly $19 billion above the $5 trillion mark it first closed above on October 14, 2026, at $342.96 a share.
A slide of about 0.4%, to near $342.60, would wipe out that buffer. Apple remains above that level, although routine headline risk is now likely enough to push it below.
Apple's statement read: "We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units. If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement."
Bloomberg confirmed the problem with more than half a dozen customers through photos and support records. Apple has not given a unit count, a cause, or a timeline for a fix.

Owners describe a crunching sound when they unfold the phone, a crack along the center crease, and a white patch on the right side of the screen. Some of the crack photos circulating online appear to be AI-generated, which makes any count harder to trust.
You do not need AppleCare+ to get a replacement. Stock is limited, though, and some owners are still waiting, so the fix could turn into a supply problem of its own.
iFixit gave the Duo a preliminary repairability score of 5 out of 10, its best for a foldable. The teardown also found a stress hotspot where the screen's curved fold presses down on the hinge's center support bar, near where breaks have been reported.
Kyle Wiens, who wrote the teardown, said that "a manufacturing variance or grain of sand can kill the fragile display panel" the hinge protects. That is a theory, and Apple has not confirmed it.
Out of warranty, Apple charges $999 to repair the inner screen. That price is why the free-replacement window matters so much to every owner.
Crossing below $5 trillion would leave Apple's cash flow unchanged, although round numbers drive headlines, and headlines drive short-term trading.
Apple trades at about 45 times earnings, with a free cash flow yield of 1.97%. Free cash flow yield is the cash the business generates as a share of its market value. A price that high assumes Apple's new product cycles keep succeeding.
iPhone revenue reached $54.25 billion in fiscal third-quarter 2026, up from $44.58 billion a year earlier. The Duo was supposed to extend that run, so a flaw in its first week hits the growth story investors are paying for.
NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) rose 2.39% to $216.00, which puts its value at $5.215 trillion, about $196 billion ahead of Apple.
Apple also revealed a redesigned iPad mini with an 8.5-inch OLED display. It starts at $699, up from $599, and preorders open on October 28, the same day as Apple's "Pro and tell" event in Los Angeles.
Apple reports fiscal fourth-quarter results after the close on November 2. Either date gives Apple a chance to name a cause and say how many units are affected.
Apple's core business looks largely protected from the problem. As stated, the defect affects a small number of units of one new model. The iPhone 17 lineup that drove fiscal 2026 growth is not affected.
At $1,999, the Duo is a niche product inside a much larger iPhone business, so even a messy launch is unlikely to materially reduce earnings.
The bigger risk is if Apple stays quiet. If the company gets to the November 2 report without naming a cause or a fix, a small defect becomes a question about whether premium prices still buy premium reliability.
If Apple closes below $342.60, stays there through the November 2 report, and has still said nothing about the cause, the market is treating the defect as more than a minor problem, and this view would be wrong.

Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals, one of China’s largest drug makers, reported a 20.55 per cent rise in third-quarter revenue to 8.95 billion yuan (US$1.34 billion), beating analyst estimates of 8.55 billion yuan amid stronger innovative drug sales.

articles.title_orig: China’s economy may never overtake America — and it’s all due to an ill-fated 47-year-old policy
articles.title_zh: China’s economy may never overtake America — and it’s all due to an ill-fated 47-year-old policy
articles.content_orig:
Just one child doomed China’s hopes of overtaking the US.
The Middle Kingdom, once a surging economic growth engine expected to eclipse the US economy in just a few years, is not expected to outgrow the US until the 2040s now — if it does at all.
And it’s largely down to China’s 1979 One Child Policy , which is devastating growth, according to Yi Fuxian, a Chinese demographer at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
Plummeting birth rates and economic problems have erased the 6+% per year growth that China reported before the COVID-19 pandemic.
Many economists in both China and the West were taken in by the Chinese Communist Party’s inflated official figures, which massively overestimated the country’s consumer power, Fuxian said.
It comes as a Goldman Sachs study found that China’s population began shrinking in 2022 , just 13 years after that of neighboring Japan. And its decline is on track to be far steeper, dramatically damaging the country’s economic prospects, the Financial Times reported .
China has a GDP of $21.6 trillion — just two-thirds the size of the US economy.
Yi told The Post that official Chinese statistics have systematically inflated the country’s birthrates and total population figures going back decades.
While official reports claim China has a population of over 1.4 billion, Yi calculates that the true figure in 2020 was “under 1.28 billion,” at least 130 million lower than reported.
India actually surpassed China as the world’s most populous nation years earlier than officially recognized, according to Yi, author of the 2007 book, “Big Country with an Empty Nest,” which criticized China’s one-child policies.
The US, the third most populous country in the world, has 342 million people — about a quarter the population of China.
Yi argues that China’s population actually began shrinking in 2018, four years earlier than Goldman Sachs’ estimate, and more than a decade before the official projection of 2031 to 2034.
Most of this can be attributed to China’s notorious One Child Policy , instituted to limit Chinese families to one child per mother, over fears of spiraling population growth and widespread poverty.
While the policy was relaxed to two children per couple in 2016 and three children in 2021, China’s total fertility rate remains one of the lowest in the world .
China is no longer poor — officially 0% of the population is in extreme poverty, compared to 88% 40 years ago.
But it’s also not rich; the per capita GDP is about $13,800 per year, about 15% of that in the US.
Turkey, Russia and Kazakhstan are all richer than China by that measure.
The country’s total fertility rate fell below the 2.1 replacement level in 1991 and continued to plummet, dropping below 1.0 and now estimated to be just 0.8 births per woman, according to Yi.
Last year saw a record low of just 8 million live births in China. The much smaller US, by contrast, had 3.6 million births.
Yi also blames the economic reforms of China’s former Premier Zhu Rongji in the 1990s, for causing “many problems” that slowed down China’s economic growth and race to catch up with the US.
Decades of strict birth restrictions and fiscal centralization severely curtailed household disposable income in China, to roughly 42-44% of GDP.
In contrast, in the US, that figure is over 70% of GDP.
While this may have helped China’s economy in the short term, allowing it to flood the US with cheap imported goods, in the long run, it may have signed the CCP’s suicide note, according to Yi.
Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.
Children function as “super-consumers,” driving much of household spending, he explained.
With China missing several full generations worth of children, this severely crippled Chinese domestic consumption, he argued.
To offset weak domestic consumption, China became heavily dependent on manufacturing exports, an unsustainable real estate bubble, and state-subsidized industrial overcapacity, he explained.
Those policies, “killed China’s economy, the population and the economy — and also killed America’s manufacturing,” Yi said.
China is now one of the oldest countries in the world, with a rapidly shrinking labor pool and aging population. The median age is expected to reach 59 by 2050, compared to 44 in the US.
This means Beijing may never catch up with the US economically — and worse, could face a long-term economic deceleration, Yi argued.
Yi puts the over-optimistic predictions about China’s economic growth down to mainstream economists and Chinese government-aligned institutions relying on fabricated data — assuming China’s population would soon grow five times larger than the US.
This played into the popular narrative that “the East is rising while the West is declining,” he said, while the truth is very different.
“By 2029 to 2035, China will lag behind the US across all major demographic and growth metrics,” Yi said.
However, for pro-democracy activists who might hope that this demographic time bomb could topple the CCP, Yi has a warning.
Contrary to Western expectations that economic development would foster a pro-democracy middle class, China’s rapid aging has depleted it of the young population required to drive political activism.
Just 16% of China is aged 15 to 29, down from 31% at the time of China’s last mass-democracy movement in 1989, which culminated in the communists’ brutal crackdown in Tiananmen Square.
An aging, risk-averse China is far more likely to support a centralized strongman who will safeguard pensions and social stability, Yi explained.

articles.title_orig: U.K. charges 2 men arrested over alleged Iran-linked terror plot against RAF Fairford air base used by U.S.
articles.title_zh: U.K. charges 2 men arrested over alleged Iran-linked terror plot against RAF Fairford air base used by U.S.
articles.content_orig:
London — Two men have been charged with serious security offenses in Britain after being arrested in connection with the incident last month near RAF Fairford, the air base in England that had been used by the U.S. military to launch strikes on Iran, the U.K. Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said Tuesday.
Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, and Nouman Essghir, 24, both British nationals and London residents, were charged under the 2023 National Security Act.
Abdulkarim was charged with "assisting a foreign intelligence service" in September and "engaging in conduct that was likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service in carrying out U.K.-related activities."
The CPS said Essghir was charged with a national security offense after he "approached or was in the vicinity of a prohibited place and his conduct was for a purpose that he knew, or having regards to other matters known to him ought reasonably to have known, was prejudicial to the safety or interests of the United Kingdom."
Both men were arrested last week on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service in a suspected plot targeting the Fairford air base in England.
Abdulkarim was arrested by Counter Terror Police under the National Security Act last week, along with another 25-year-old man — a British-Iranian dual national who was released on bail pending further investigation.
Police are still investigating a suspected terror plot against Fairford after five men were initially detained on Sept. 27 near the base in western England. All five of those men were also released on bail, but police said they remained under investigation and would be monitored.
U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said the government believes Iran "played a part" in the incident at the base, which prompted the U.S. Air Force to remove all of its B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford . The base had been home to U.S. long-range bombers for many years, and it was used during the war with Iran to launch strikes on the Islamic Republic.
Residents of a nearby town were evacuated from their homes near the base as armed police and bomb-disposal experts searched the area on Sept. 27. They found gasoline in three vans that had been driven by the five initial suspects, parked close to an entrance to the base, but no explosives.
Iranian officials have said repeatedly that any bases used to attack the country would be considered legitimate targets. The Iranian Embassy in London, however, said in a previous statement that the regime "categorically rejects and strongly condemns the recent unfounded and malicious speculations published by some British individuals and media outlets attempting to link Iran" to the incident.
Police said Tuesday that six men remain free on bail in relation to the incident, four of whom were arrested on Sept. 27 — all U.K. nationals and London residents in their 20s — and two others who were detained subsequently, including the 25-year-old dual U.K.-Iranian national who was detained on Oct. 1.

articles.title_zh: iPhone 18e Could Get Two Key Upgrades While Keeping 60Hz Display
articles.content_orig:
Apple's upcoming iPhone 18e model will retain a 60Hz display but could gain an upgraded front-facing camera, according to the leaker known as "Digital Chat Station."
In a new post on Weibo, the leaker said that the device will feature a 6.12-inch OLED display using low-temperature polycrystalline silicon (LTPS) technology, the A20 chip, and a single 48-megapixel rear camera. They were less definitive about the front-facing camera, saying it could be upgraded to 24 megapixels.
The specifications suggest that the iPhone 18e will offer no major display or rear camera hardware upgrades over the previous two generations. Both the iPhone 16e and iPhone 17e feature approximately 6.1-inch ‌OLED‌ displays with a 60Hz refresh rate and a single 48-megapixel rear camera. The post does not detail the rear camera's sensor or lens, so smaller hardware changes remain possible.
The A20 chip would represent a more significant upgrade. Like the A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro , the A20 is expected to use a 2nm manufacturing process , bringing notable performance and power efficiency improvements over the iPhone 17e 's 3nm A19 chip. It would also bring the device into line with the upcoming standard iPhone 18 , which is expected to use the same chip .
The front-facing camera claim is less clear. Digital Chat Station specified 24 megapixels, although it is unclear whether this refers to a new camera or is a mistaken reference to the 18-megapixel Center Stage camera introduced with the iPhone 17 lineup. A 24-megapixel camera was widely rumored before those devices launched. Either resolution would represent an upgrade over the 12-megapixel front camera used by the iPhone 16e and ‌iPhone 17e‌.
Digital Chat Station previously claimed that the iPhone 18e would retain a 60Hz LTPS display. An earlier report from Korea suggested that an LTPO display capable of supporting 120Hz ProMotion could reach the entry-level iPhone with the "iPhone 19e" in 2028.
The iPhone 18e is expected to launch in spring 2027 , alongside the standard ‌iPhone 18‌ and iPhone Air 2.
